name: Iconography
summary: The icon font, the one style every icon is drawn in, its sizes and colors, and when an icon needs a name.
description: Icons are glyphs of Material Symbols Outlined, an icon font: a component names an icon by its ligature name and the font draws it. The font is variable; the system fixes its axes (fill, weight, grade, optical size) to a single style, so every icon looks the same in every component. The Figma library has no icon tokens: the font and its axes (font.icon.*) are the design system's additions, read directly by components. Icons take their size from the size scale and their color from the text next to them.

rules.name: Icon font
rules.text: Icons are glyphs of Material Symbols Outlined. A component names an icon by its ligature name (arrow_forward, delete), and the font draws it.

rules.name: One style
rules.text: Every icon is drawn in one style: outlined (fill off), light weight, normal grade, optical size 20. The axes are fixed for the whole system, never chosen per component.

rules.name: Size
rules.text: An icon in a control takes a size from the size scale (Spacing and sizing foundation), per control size: size.2 (16 px) at extra small and small, size.3 (20 px) at medium, size.4 (24 px) at large. The glyph fills a square of that size.

rules.name: Color
rules.text: An icon takes the color of the text next to it, or the icon role of its context (global.icon.*, which aliases that text color), so it follows every emphasis, intent, state and mode.

rules.name: Decorative or named
rules.text: Next to a visible label, an icon repeats the label and is hidden from assistive technology. Alone in a control (icon button), the icon is the only visible content and the control carries a name describing its action.

rules.name: Web font loading
rules.text: The fonts.css of the web reference implementation requests only the instance with the fixed axes. The font is loaded with display=block, so the ligature names do not flash as text while it loads.

specimens.name: Icon style
specimens.description: Every icon the component examples use, drawn in the system style, and the axis values.

specimens.name: Icon sizes
specimens.description: An icon at each size the controls use.

guidelines.text: An icon next to a visible label is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; an icon alone in a control is non-text content, so the control has a name that describes its purpose.

An icon that carries meaning on its own contrasts at least 3:1 with its background; icons take the color of their text (a known issue lists the error states where that text falls under 4.5:1; the icons still reach 3:1).
Icons complement color: when color shows an intent or a state, a label or a distinct icon shows it too.
Hide the glyph with aria-hidden="true": an icon-font glyph is written as its ligature name, which would otherwise be read.
Icons that convey meaning grow with the text when people raise the text size.
A decorative icon gets a null content description; an icon that is the only content of an action gets a description naming the action.

changelog.note: Fix, no decision changed: the web-font-loading statement names the fonts.css of the web reference implementation, no longer published in @quantum-ds/components (the package ships the specs only).

Breaking: the semantic icon group icon.*, invented by the repository, is removed; components alias the icon font tokens font.icon.* directly (the design system's additions, unchanged values), and icon sizes come from size.2 / 3 / 4 instead of control.icon-size.*. No visual change.
Initial draft: the icon font and its fixed style as they are, specified once (no token changes).
